id: The Ten Tenors-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: The Ten Tenors
venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
The world’s longest-running classical crossover act celebrates 30 years of magnificent singing. The music ensemble The Ten Tenors was formed in 1995. Since then, they have toured over 3,500 shows across 34 countries. Their signature brand of music featuring 10-part harmonies has been enjoyed by more than 100 million people worldwide. 

The Ten Tenors have become renowned for their dynamic, choreographed performances. Their skilful technique lets them transition seamlessly between operatic arias, soulful ballads, chart-topping pop, and rock songs. They have shared the stage with iconic artists including Lionel Richie, Rod Stewart, Andrea Bocelli, Willie Nelson, Alanis Morissette and Christina Aguilera. They have also appeared extensively on TV. 

Following a four-year hiatus, The Ten Tenors make a grand return to New Zealand in March. The breathtaking 30th anniversary show will feature their signature 10-part vocal harmonies.

id: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button The Musical-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button The Musical
venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Every second counts. That’s the theme of The Curious Case of Benjamin Button. Having taken London and New York by storm, the hit musical is now making its way to Wellington, New Zealand. 

Described by WhatsOnStage as “The best British musical in decades” the show is an enchantingly beautiful and truly unordinary story. It follows Benjamin Button who is born old and bound to the fate of growing younger each day, Benjamin wants nothing more than to live a little life. But will he ever find a place to belong?   

The Olivier Award-winning musical is based on the 1922 short story by F Scott Fitzgerald. The story also inspired a 2008 movie. Now for the first time out of Broadway and the West End it travels to Australasia and Wellington has scored the premier. It brings a big heart, a foot-stomping score, and 15 remarkable actor-musicians who, among them, play 30 instruments. Get ready for a sweeping live score and a show epic in scale but intimate in feeling.

id: An Evening with Mary Beard: Talking Classics-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: An Evening with Mary Beard: Talking Classics
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Join English classicist and historian Dame Mary Beard in Wellington for a night packed with witty stories and surprising facts. An Evening with Mary Beard: Talking Classics plays at The Opera House in Wellington. The show is built around her new book, ‘Talking Classics: The Shock of the Old’. A guest host joins Mary and will round out the evening with a Q&A. If you have burning questions about Roman emperors or 4,000-year-old bread, now is the time to have them answered.   

Mary has made a career around refusing to let the ancient world stay ancient. She’s authored more than 20 books, including ‘SPQR’ and ‘Emperor of Rome’. These books helped popularise Roman history while staying true to her academic roots (she had a 40-year career at the University of Cambridge). She’s appeared on television programmes from Roman history documentaries to ‘The Grand Tour’.   

Expect an unpretentious and informative evening. On your way out, pick up a copy of ‘Talking Classics’. Get the book signed by Mary, and leave feeling more knowledgeable than when you walked in.

id: An Evening with Guenther Steiner-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: An Evening with Guenther Steiner
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Former Haas F1 boss Guenther Steiner brings his new live show, ‘No Team Orders’, to The Opera House in Wellington. The 2026 season gave Formula 1 new cars, new rules, and new teams on the grid. Days after the final race, Guenther unpacks it all. He shares his take on which teams cracked the rule changes first and which young drivers stood out. Expect blunt opinions and stories from inside the paddock. 

Guenther has spent more than 30 years in motorsport. He started in rallying, working with drivers such as Colin McRae, a three-time Rally New Zealand winner. He later ran Jaguar Racing in Formula 1. Then he built the Haas team from scratch and led it for a decade. You might have seen him on the Netflix series ‘Formula 1: Drive to Survive’, where his colourful honesty made him a fan favourite. He famously claims he has never watched it. He has also written two books, ‘Surviving to Drive’ and ‘Unfiltered’. Today, he is CEO of the Red Bull KTM Tech3 MotoGP team. 

The evening is a live conversation on stage, followed by an audience Q&A. Bring a question of your own and put it to Guenther directly. Join whether you’ve just discovered him or you’ve followed Formula 1 since you were a wee one. Book your seats, and leave with enough insider secrets to impress at the work Christmas party.

id: The Guilty Feminist Podcast: Live-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: The Guilty Feminist Podcast: Live
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
If you‘ve ever said “I‘m a feminist but...”, The Guilty Feminist Podcast: Live is for you. Host and comedian Deborah Frances-White returns to Wellington with her new series, ‘The Road to Gilead Project‘. Settle into a seat at The Opera House to watch a podcast happen live on stage. In this series, Deborah talks with comedians, artists, authors, academics, and activists. Expect equal parts comedy and deep-dive discussion. 

The Road to Gilead Project takes its name from Gilead, the nightmare state from Margaret Atwood‘s ‘The Handmaid‘s Tale‘. Deborah thinks some of today‘s headlines are starting to read a lot like the book. Around the world, hard-won rights for women and LGBTQ+ communities are being challenged. So how do you get off the road to Gilead? Deborah‘s answer is a joyful resistance, with plenty of laughs along the way. 

Since 2015, Deborah has turned the fear of being a ‘bad feminist’ into a multi-award-winning podcast with more than 200 million downloads. Guests confess the gap between their principles and their everyday habits. Nobody is perfect, and that‘s the point. Come along to experience everything you love about The Guilty Feminist, with a new focus.
